We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 5 reactions to synthesize target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have identified a TBS deprotection template (29646) that removes TBS protecting group: converts C-Si to OH. The target appears to have no TBS group; but maybe intermediate has TBS protected alcohol. So step 5 (final) could be deprotection of TBS to give free OH.

We also have HWE/Still-Gennari template (682444) that forms an alkene with ester? Actually that template seems to convert an alcohol + alkene? The product is an ester with double bond? The template: [#8:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:6])/[CH;D2;+0:3]=[CH;D2;+0:5]/[C:4]>>... This is a HWE forming an alkene attached to a carboxylate. So step could be formation of the conjugated diene chain with terminal carboxylic acid (C(O)=O). So we can use Still-Gennari to form the (Z)-alkene? The target has a trans? Not sure.

We also have DIBAL-H reduction to aldehyde? Not yet.

We need 5 steps: maybe 1) Protect secondary alcohol with TBS. 2) Form side chain via Still-Gennari (HWE) to attach unsaturated ester. 3) Reduce ester to aldehyde via DIBAL-H. 4) Perform Wittig/HWE to install further alkene? Actually target has two conjugated double bonds: C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O (a triene with terminal carboxylic acid). Could be built via sequential HWE? Maybe first form the terminal alkene with carboxylic acid via Still-Gennari from aldehyde and phosphonate. Then reduce to alcohol? Actually target has a primary alcohol (CH2OH) attached to the first double bond? The SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O. Let's parse: a cyclohexane with two OH groups (one free, one O-alkyl linking to side chain). The side chain: O-CH (attached to cyclohexane) then /C=C(CO)/C (i.e., a double bond with a CH2OH substituent). Then continues C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O (a conjugated diene ending with carboxylic acid). So overall side chain is: O-CH-CH= C(CO) -C- C= C- C= C- C(=O)O. That's a polyene with terminal COOH and a primary alcohol on the first double bond.

We could retrosynthesize: break at the ether O to give alcohol on cyclohexane and side chain alcohol (protected). So step 5: deprotect TBS on side chain alcohol? Actually side chain primary alcohol could be protected as TBS during earlier steps.

Plan steps:

Step 1 (final): Deprotect TBS from side chain primary alcohol to give free CH2OH. Use template 29646 (TBS removal). So precursor is same molecule but with OSi(tBu)(Me)2 instead of OH at that position. So precursor SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(C[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O? Actually TBS attached to primary alcohol: CH2OTBS. So side chain would be ...C=C(C[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)/C. Need to generate.

Step 2: The side chain primary alcohol (now protected) could be formed via reduction of aldehyde (DIBAL-H) from aldehyde precursor. So we need aldehyde at that position: CHO. Use DIBAL-H to reduce ester? Actually DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, not aldehyde to alcohol. Wait DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde; then further reduction to alcohol via NaBH4 maybe. But we have DIBAL-H step in guidance: reduces esters/nitriles to aldehydes. So we could have precursor as ester, apply DIBAL-H to get aldehyde, then later reduce to alcohol? But we need alcohol, not aldehyde. Could use DIBAL-H to reduce ester to aldehyde, then later maybe use something else to convert aldehyde to alcohol (e.g., NaBH4 not in list). Maybe we can use DIBAL-H in reverse retrosynthesis: we have alcohol, we can think of it coming from aldehyde via reduction (not DIBAL). Not available. Could use DIBAL-H to go from ester to aldehyde, then later to alcohol via something else not given. Might be okay to have 5 steps including DIBAL-H for another part (the terminal carboxylic acid maybe from ester). Actually terminal COOH could be derived from ester via hydrolysis (not in list). Could be from HWE forming ester then hydrolysis later (not listed). But we have HWE that forms ester directly.

Thus propose route:

1) Deprotect TBS (template 29646) -> target.

2) Remove TBS earlier: we need precursor with TBS-protected primary alcohol.

3) That precursor could be obtained by Still-Gennari HWE (template 682444) forming the conjugated diene with terminal ester (CO2R). The product of HWE is an ester with double bond. Our precursor after step 2 still has TBS-protected primary alcohol and an ester at terminal (maybe methyl ester). Then later we can hydrolyze ester to acid (not in list). But maybe we can consider that the terminal COOH is derived from aldehyde via oxidation (not listed). Could be from oxidation of primary alcohol (not listed). Hmm.

Maybe we can design 5 steps using given reactions: TBS protection, Still-Gennari, DIBAL-H, HWE, etc.

But we need to output a route JSON with 5 reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We have IDs: 29646 (TBS deprotection). 682444 (Still-Gennari). Need template for TBS protection (introducing TBS). Not yet searched. Let's search for functional_groups_formed: t-butyldimethylsilyl? Actually protecting adds TBS group, breaking O-H. So functional_groups_broken: aliphatic hydroxyls; formed: t-butyldimethylsilyl. Search.
